---
title: Build your graph
description: What each of dockg's seven derive sources reads from your repo, how to control which files get ingested, and how to read the corpus back with stats.
---

import { Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`dockg build` reads what is already on disk and writes a graph. Nothing here requires you to
change a document first. This page covers what it reads, how to control what it reads, and how to
interpret what comes back.

## Before you start

You should have run `dockg build` once — see [Get started](/dockg/get-started/) — and have a
`graph.ttl` to look at.

## The seven derive sources

Every source is on by default. They are hermetic: no network, no credentials, no spend.

| Source | Reads | Emits |
|---|---|---|
| `frontmatter` | Frontmatter fields and the `kg` block | Titles, descriptions, creators, dates, subjects, concepts, iiRDS typing |
| `sections` | Every heading | A `dockg:Section` node per heading, with level and sibling order |
| `links` | Markdown links between documents | `dcterms:references` edges, and `dockg:brokenLink` for unresolvable targets |
| `tags` | `tags` and `keywords` | `dcterms:subject` pointing at `skos:Concept` nodes |
| `images` | Image references | `schema:image` |
| `code` | Fenced code blocks | `dockg:codeLanguage` per language used |
| `provenance` | Frontmatter dates and authors, plus git history | PROV-O entities, activities, agents, and qualified attribution |

Turn any of them off in config:

```yaml title="dockg.config.yaml"
build:
  derive: [frontmatter, sections, links, tags]
```

`build.derive` is config-only. A graph built with different derive rules is a different graph, so
it should not depend on how someone typed the command.

<Aside type="note" title="Only `provenance` touches anything outside your files">
  It shells out to git for committer history. Under the default `provenance.git: auto` a repo
  without git history warns and continues; the build still exits 0.
</Aside>

## Control what gets ingested

<Steps>

1. **Set your inputs.** With no config file dockg ingests `**/*.md` — which includes
   `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and any Markdown in `test/`. That is rarely what you want past
   the first run.

   ```yaml title="dockg.config.yaml"
   version: 1
   inputs:
     - "docs/**/*.md"
   exclude:
     - "**/node_modules/**"
     - "docs/drafts/**"
   ```

   <Aside type="caution" title="Globs resolve against the working directory">
     Not against the config file. Run dockg from the repo root, or it matches nothing:

     ```
     dockg: No input files matched: docs/**/*.md (cwd: /repo/docs)
     ```
   </Aside>

2. **Set a real `baseIri`.** IRIs are the graph's stable identity, and changing the base later
   rewrites every subject in the file.

   ```yaml title="dockg.config.yaml"
   baseIri: https://docs.example.com/kg/
   ```

3. **Rebuild and confirm the document count changed as you expected.**

   ```sh
   dockg build
   ```

   ```
   Wrote kg/graph.ttl (4 docs, 139 triples)
   ```

</Steps>

## Read the corpus back

```sh
dockg stats
```

```
Triples:    139
Documents:  4
Sections:   8
Concepts:   5
References: 6

Most connected:
  docs/configuration.md (5)
  docs/getting-started.md (3)

Orphan docs (0):
  (none)

Broken internal links (1):
  docs/no-frontmatter.md -> missing.md

Broken section refs (1):
  docs/getting-started.md -> #missing-heading

Coverage:
  title        4/4  100.0%
  description  1/4  25.0%
  prefLabel    1/4  25.0%
```

**Most connected** are your hub documents — the ones whose removal or rename hurts most.

**Orphan docs** have no inbound or outbound `dcterms:references`. A genuine orphan is usually
either unreachable content or a page everybody links to from a nav config that dockg cannot see.

**Broken internal links** point at files that do not exist. If your corpus links by published site
route rather than file path, expect many of these and see below — they are a configuration gap,
not a corpus defect.

**Broken section refs** are `kg.sections` keys matching no heading, almost always a renamed
heading.

**Coverage** is the fraction of documents carrying each field. A low first number is the normal
starting point, not a failing grade.

<Aside type="caution" title="dockg does not parse MDX">
  Markdown parsing covers headings, prose links, and frontmatter in `.mdx` files, but JSX is
  treated as raw text. Links inside components — `<LinkCard href="…">` and similar — **do not
  become graph edges.** If your site is MDX-based and component-heavy, your reference counts and
  orphan list will understate reality.
</Aside>

## What you have now

A graph over exactly the files you intended, with a reading of how connected and how annotated
they are. Nothing is enforced yet.
